newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Almost 40 dead in three days of Colombia violence.
newsitem.headline: Almost 40 dead in three days of Colombia violence.

text.p: Three leftist rebels died in a firefight with the army in southern Colombia early on Sunday, military sources said, taking to almost 40 the number of people killed in politically-motivated violence in three days.

In the latest fighting, counterinsurgency troops killed three Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) guerrillas in a jungle region of Putumayo province on Sunday morning, Gen. Jose Miranda Garcia said.

At least 36 other people killed since Friday in northern Cesar and Magadalena provinces and in northwest Antioquia province were thought to be the victims of a wave of attacks by right-wing paramilitary groups, police said.
The so-called Peasant Self-Defence Group of Cordoba and Uraba, a paramilitary group operating in northern Colombia, has frequently targeted those suspected of sympathising with leftist guerrillas.
The first killings were reported before dawn on Friday when a gang gunned down five people in two working-class districts of Cesar's main town, Valledupar, police said.

Shortly before midnight on Friday, eight people from two families were called from their homes in Nutibara and killed in front of neighbours. Hours later, five more people were shot dead by drive-by assassins as they played cards outside a bar in Apartado in Antioquia's banana-growing region of Uraba.

On Saturday, seven people, four from one family, were murdered by well-armed, unidentified killers in a village near Valledupar and four men were pulled out of a truck at a makeshift road-block near Aguachica, also in Cesar, and shot, a police spokesman said.

In neighbouring Magadalena seven people were killed in three separate attacks on Saturday. Witnesses blamed the deaths on paramiltary groups, the RCN radio network said, but the reports could not be confirmed by police on Sunday.
